slides.title: What is Better - Cline or Claude Code
slides.text: What is Better - Cline or Claude Code ? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uIKmG3M0X3M "Cline: The MCP-first IDE" - interview, Latent Space (July 16, 2025) Cline is an open-source coding agent , mainly a VS Code extension , soon expanding to JetBrains, Neovim, and CLI It acts as infrastructure for agentic systems , modular, and designed to build any agent, not just for coding Users give Cline a task; it automates workflows across terminals, editors, browsers, and connects to "MCP" Cline pioneered the "Plan and Act" paradigm Workflow is highly collaborative in plan mode, then shifts to automation in act mode, with user oversight ( auto-approve or step-by-step ). Cline sought to simplify user experience, making advanced agent workflows accessible and intuitive Though mainly for coding, Cline is used in varied domains ( marketing, slide generation, data analysis ) due to its general, modular nature; Examples include automating presentations and integrating with tools like Reddit or Slack via MCP servers. Coding is seen as the highest-value application for LLMs/agents; Despite MCP ecosystem growth into non-coding areas, most value and use is with developer tasks. Marketplace for MCPs in Cline, listing 150+ servers with significant usage. Cline emphasizes transparency (what the model is doing, errors, prompt context) for better user control and quick course correction. You can run various LLMs (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, ...) - thus ensure performance and low cost Fully autonomous tools for rapid prototyping, high-insight agentic tools for complex/creative coding; Both agentic power and transparency - hybrid workflows - some users oversee every step, others "auto-approve" and review results afterward. Cline support architecture design for senior engineers and coding / explanation for junior level Cline is often preferred by professionals who value control, system-level integration, and safety in complex code changes. Claude Code also allows pausing for reviews (in CLAUDE.md or similar project files, or explicitly in the prompt). But ... there are credible user reports that Claude Code sometimes misses subtle bugs or hallucinates - more than when using “Claude in Cline” Users recommend pairing “Claude” models with Cline for best-of-both-worlds: Cline’s workflow features and Claude’s reasoning power CheatSheet for Claude Code: https://github.com/Njengah/claude-code-cheat-sheet Please Pause The Video - and provide your comments/opinion under the video (Terminal based vs Cline)

slides.title: Energy-Based Transformers (EBTs) Energy-Based Transformers (EBTs) are significantly
slides.text: Energy-Based Transformers (EBTs) Energy-Based Transformers (EBTs) are significantly different from standard Transformer architecture EBTs substitute standard feed-forward direct mapping of input to output by an iterative optimization process, trying minimize "Energy" EBTs assign an energy value (a scalar representing unnormalized probability or compatibility) to each (input, prediction) pair . The goal is to find the prediction that minimizes this energy , which is interpreted as the most compatible or likely outcome During inference, EBTs iteratively refine predictions using gradient descent to minimize the energy, rather than making a one-shot prediction. This process is analogous to “thinking” or “reasoning” over possible outputs EBTs implement System 2 Thinking - slow, analytical, and deliberate reasoning by spending more computation on harder problems. This is achieved by allowing the model to perform multiple steps of energy minimization , dynamically allocating more resources when needed In experiments, this approach led to 29% better performance on language tasks compared to advanced feed-forward Transformers EBTs combine generation and verification in a single model . The energy function acts as both the predictor and the verifier, enabling the model to check the compatibility of its own predictions as part of the inference process EBTs are designed to be agnostic to input modality and problem type. They have demonstrated strong results in both discrete (text) and continuous (vision) domains, outperforming not only feed-forward Transformers but also Diffusion Transformers in image denoising tasks, with fewer forward passes required EBTs show superior scaling properties : they achieve up to 35% higher scaling rates with respect to data size , batch volume, parameters, FLOPs, and network depth compared to state-of-the-art Transformers They also exhibit better generalization , especially on out of distribution data, suggesting a more robust understanding of tasks beyond memorization https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2507.02092 - paper

slides.title: LLMS match patterns without understanding LLMS match patterns
slides.text: LLMS match patterns without understanding LLMS match patterns without understanding https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jxB-lQyAAxU Research from Harvard and MIT tests whether AI models truly understand the world (create world models) or just memorize patterns Researchers trained transformer models to predict planetary positions with high accuracy, then fine-tuned them to predict gravitational forces - the underlying physical principle that governs orbital motion. Models achieved 99%+ accuracy predicting orbital positions, but failed catastrophically when asked to predict gravitational forces Using symbolic regression, researchers discovered the models learned nonsensical, non-physical formulas; Each solar system configuration produced different arbitrary "laws" - no universal understanding Instead of discovering Newton's elegant F = GMm/r² law, models created complex, wiggly mathematical functions that Perfectly fit the training data through overfitting, Had no relationship to actual physics, Couldn't generalize to related tasks, Were essentially sophisticated memorization Testing Commercial Models (GPT-4, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro) using in-context learning - all failed similarly, despite having physics knowledge in training data, they couldn't apply it coherently. Models defaulted to simple, incorrect heuristics Knowing ≠ Understanding ≠ Applying Even models trained on all of Wikipedia's physics content failed to spontaneously access and apply coherent world models when needed This suggests current AI lacks genuine intelligence and operates through pattern matching rather than principled understanding The research provides strong evidence that current foundation models, regardless of architecture (Transformers, LSTMs, Mamba), are sophisticated pattern matchers without true world understanding - calling into question claims about emerging intelligence in AI systems

slides.title: Meta META is building Microkernel OS A microkernel
slides.text: Meta META is building Microkernel OS A microkernel system communicates through message-passing, reducing the size of trusted code in kernel space. This improves modularity, reliability, and (potentially) upgradability. // Linux - Monolithic sys_read() { // Kernel-space file system call // Direct disk I/O and scheduling // Memory mapped file buffers } // MetaOS - Microkernel Style sys_read() { send_msg(FS_SERVICE, "read") } // FS_SERVICE (runs in userspace) read_handler() { // Handles logic // Requests disk I/O through another IPC } Windows OS - Monolithic Linux - Kernel + multiple utilities/processes communicating using pipes, signals, etc. Microkernel OS - even less Monolithic Meta plans Manhattan-sized AI centers Prometheus : Located in New Albany, Ohio, this is slated to deliver over 1 gigawatt (GW) of power capacity, with operations expected to commence in 2026. Hyperion : Planned for Richmond Parish, Louisiana, this facility is designed to scale up to 5 GW of capacity over several years, making it one of the largest AI projects of its kind

slides.title: AWS IDE Kiro Kiro - AI-powered IDE from
slides.text: AWS IDE Kiro Kiro - AI-powered IDE from AWS It is a customized fork of VS Code https://kiro.dev It uses Claude Sonnet 4. But not supporting Gemini, Ollama, OpenRouter, ... slides.title: Cline System Prompt & Rules Files I am
slides.text: Cline System Prompt & Rules Files I am using Cline VSCode extension as AI Coding Assistant for LLMs like Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, etc. Cline has its own system prompt that defines its behaviour. It is baked into Cline and can not be seen. But you can see it in Cline's Github: https://github.com/cline/cline : https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/src/core/prompts/system.ts There used to be the "custom instructions" section in settings. But it was removed in recent versions. It is possible to modify Cline's behaviour by adding a " .clinerules " file to the root of any project. Or a " .clinerules/ " directory with multiple .md files inside to separate rules for different aspects like formatting, documentation, or testing Cline’s newer releases include a popover UI (under the chat input) for selecting which rules from your .clinerules/ files and folders are active at any given moment. https://github.com/nickbaumann98/cline_docs/tree/main https://docs.cline.bot/getting-started/for-new-coders The .clineignore file is a project-level configuration for the Cline VSCode extension, modeled after .gitignore. It lets you specify which files and directories Cline should ignore during codebase analysis and AI operations. This helps keep responses relevant, block access to specific files (e.g., .env, secrets.txt), or folders (like node_modules/, dist/, build/) or file types ( like *.csv, *.log). This reduces processing time by excluding large or irrelevant files or directories (like dependencies or auto-generated files). To create the file, just copy your .gitignore - or ask some LLM (like Perplexity) to give you .clineignore file for specific type of a project (for example, for working with python and jupyter and doing data science / machine learning)

slides.title: AI and Learning - Derek Muller https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0xS68sl2D70 Why
slides.text: AI and Learning - Derek Muller https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0xS68sl2D70 Why Educational "Revolutions" Keep Failing (1920 .. 2010). The problem isn't access to information - it's getting people to engage in the hard work of learning How Learning Actually Works: Daniel Kahneman's "System 1" (fast, automatic) vs "System 2" (slow, effortful) thinking framework. Real learning happens when System 2 builds knowledge through repeated practice , which then becomes automatic in System 1 Expertise comes from domain-specific knowledge structures , not general "thinking skills" AI's Role in Education: Positive - can provide immediate feedback and personalized tutoring; Concerning - may reduce the effortful practice that's essential for learning (like using AI to write essays instead of learning to write) Education won't be "revolutionized" by technology because the fundamental challenge isn't distributing information - it's motivating people to do the hard, repetitive work of building expertise . Teachers act like "personal trainers" who create accountability and social motivation that technology alone cannot replace The talk emphasizes that learning requires struggle and effort, and AI's biggest risk is making it too easy to avoid that necessary difficulty. Derek Muller (creator of Veritasium) A B Info, Feedback Motivation, Energy, Hard Work, Repetition

slides.title: The Expert Myth - Derek Muller https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5eW6Eagr9XA Experts
slides.text: The Expert Myth - Derek Muller https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5eW6Eagr9XA Experts like chess masters don't have higher IQs or better general memory. Instead, they recognize patterns instantly through "chunking" - seeing complex configurations as single units rather than individual pieces. The Four "Must Have" Requirements for True Expertise: Many (thousands) repeated attempts with feedback Valid environment with learnable patterns (one-off and very random events can not be predicted reliably) Timely feedback Deliberate practice - you must consistently work at the edge of your ability, not just repeat comfortable tasks Examples when "Experts" perform poorly: Political pundits - perform worse than random chance; Stock fund managers fail to beat market averages 80-90% of the time; Experienced doctors perform poorly at diagnosing rare diseases; College admissions officers often perform worse than simple algorithms because they get delayed or no feedback Reaching plateau - and breaking through it via challenge and discomfort of deliberate practice Conclusion: True expertise requires thousands of hours of uncomfortable, deliberate practice in environments where patterns can be learned and feedback is immediate. Without all four criteria, you get people who seem like experts but actually aren't.

slides.title: Prisoner's Dilemma - Robert Axelrod Two individuals are
slides.text: Prisoner's Dilemma - Robert Axelrod Two individuals are arrested and interrogated separately for a crime they allegedly committed together. Each person has two options: cooperate with the other by remaining silent - or defect by betraying the other and testifying against them. If both cooperate (remain silent), they each receive a light sentence. If one defects while the other cooperates, the defector goes free while the cooperator receives a heavy sentence. If both defect, they both receive moderate sentences, which is worse than if they had both cooperated. Robert Axelrod's famous computer tournaments (1980-1984) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mScpHTIi-kM https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Axelrod_(political_scientist) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Evolution_of_Cooperation Winning Strategy: "Tit for Tat" - a simple strategy that starts by cooperating, then copies whatever the opponent did in the previous round - won both tournaments despite being the simplest entry Four Key Principles of Successful Strategies: Nice - Never defect first Forgiving - Don't hold grudges beyond the last round Retaliatory - Strike back immediately when defected against Clear - Be predictable so others can establish patterns of trust In repeated interactions, cooperation can emerge even among purely self-interested players. Nice strategies consistently outperformed nasty ones . Being "generous" (occasionally forgiving defections) helps in noisy environments . There's no single best strategy - success depends on what other strategies you're playing against. Most of life is not zero-sum - mutual cooperation can benefit everyone The findings helped explain everything from animal behavior (like impala grooming) to international relations (US-Soviet nuclear disarmament), showing how cooperation can evolve and spread even in competitive environments

slides.title: Dave Ramsey 5 Rules The 5 Wealth-Building Rules
slides.text: Dave Ramsey 5 Rules The 5 Wealth-Building Rules - by Dave Ramsey https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZCrAin5ycXA 1. Get on a Budget . Create a written plan for your money. Do a budget on paper, on purpose, before each month begins. Treat managing your personal money like you would manage money for a company. You can decide today to start budgeting and managing money well 2. Get Out of Debt . Stop borrowing money entirely ("have a plasectomy" - cut up credit cards). Recognize that debt makes you a slave to lenders. Understand that your income is your most powerful wealth-building tool. Example: A $500/month car payment invested from age 30-70 could become $5.6 million instead of making car companies rich 3. Foster High Quality Relationships . Be careful about who you spend time with because "you become who you hang around with". Your income will approximate within 10-20% of your 10 closest friends' average income over 10 years. Choose to associate with people you want to be like. Avoid people with poor financial habits and attitudes 4. Save and Invest . "In the house of the wise are stores of choice food and oil" - wise people save money. Save for emergencies because "it's gonna rain" (unexpected expenses will happen). Save and invest so you can retire with dignity. Don't rely on the government to take care of you in retirement 5. Practice Generosity . Develop a generous spirit, not just transferring funds. Generous people are more attractive, cheerful, and helpful. Be generous in everyday situations (good tips, helping others). Generosity changes everything in your life, but it's hard to give when you're broke
